SID frequency table: 192 words, low byte first. Note byte n uses entry 2n (notes $00-$5f). The even entries are semitones in NTSC tuning (C0 = 16.35 Hz at 1022727 Hz). Each odd entry is the mean of its neighbours. The last word is $ffff. The driver adds the base $9ebb as two immediates at $9992 and $9d1f.
Note lengths in music ticks, 16 words. Event bytes $c0-$cf select entry 0-15. Command $f4 adds two entries.
CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words. A larger value gives a slower tune.

CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words. Each value is 1000000 / ticks per second, for 16 to 80 ticks per second. A larger value gives a slower tune. The values assume 1 MHz: on a PAL C64 the music is 1.5% slower.
Offset of the SID registers of voice 0, 1 and 2 (0, 7, 14) in the SID copy at $31.
Offset of voice 0, 1 and 2 in the effect phase tables at $0200 and $0209 (3 phases each).
The command bytes $f0-$f9 of the tune data. The driver compares an event byte with each entry.
Handler of each command $f0-$f9: rest, restart, end, instrument, length, goto, tempo, call, return, filter.
Pointers to the 16 filter settings of command $f9.
Filter setting, 11 bytes. Bytes 0-4: step delay, cutoff high, cutoff low, resonance and routing, mode. Then 3 phases: cutoff step (x 8), step count.
Start of each tune, 114 words (tunes $00-$71). The sound request $80+n in $dc-$de starts tune n.
Tune data: bytes $00-$bf are notes, $c0-$cf select a note length, $f0-$f9 are commands with 0-2 argument bytes.

Instruments of command $f3, 12 bytes each (63 entries). Command $f3 n reads entry n at $a384+12n. Bytes 0-3: attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform with inverted pulse width high, inverted pulse width low. Bytes 4-5: effect delay, effect flags. Then 3 phases: value, length.

Work bitmap of the fight area: 8 character rows of 320 bytes (bitmap rows 14-21). The fighters are drawn here. The arena change at $8e73 also uses $a678-$b677 as 16 rows of 256 bytes and swaps it with $d000-$dfff.

Work bitmap of the fight area: 8 character rows of 320 bytes (bitmap rows 14-21), $a678-$b077. $b000-$b077 is not in the program. The fighters are drawn here. The arena change at $8e73 also uses $a678-$b677 as 16 rows of 256 bytes and swaps it with $d000-$dfff.
Columns 4-35 of each work bitmap row start at $a698+320k (256 bytes). $8cad copies them to the screen bitmap.
End of the clean copy of the fight area: rows of 320 bytes from $b078. $b000-$b3e7 is not in the program.
Columns 4-35 of bitmap row 14+k, at $b098+320k. $8c41 fills them, $8c77 copies them to the work bitmap.
Pointers to the 24 texts. The text printer at $92df draws text $80+n from entry n.

Text format: column, row, colour byte, then characters. $0d starts a new line with 3 new header bytes. The colour byte goes to screen RAM (high nibble) and colour RAM (low nibble). Other characters than A-Z and text_special_chars end the text. Text 0: "000" at row 22. No code prints text 0.
Text 1: the version "V 05 05 87". CTRL+V shows it.
Texts 2-4: "1PLR", "2PLR" and "DEMO" at row 24.
Text 5: "PAUSED". No code prints text 5.
Text 6: two digits at row 5. $8294 writes the time ($c8) or the level ($be) into them.
Texts 7 and 8: the 5-digit scores of fighter 0 and 1 at row 5.
Text 9: "YOUR END HAS COME".
Text 10: "THANKS BIG BOY".
Texts 11-23: the energy display for energy 0-12, 20 bytes each. Each has 2 lines of 6 characters. "(" and ")" draw the energy units. $82da writes the column of the fighter into byte 0 and byte 10.
The 13 characters other than A-Z that the text printer draws: 0-9, space, "(" and ")".
Font glyph of each character in text_special_chars.
Column of the energy display of fighter 0 and 1 (0 and 34).
Five score digits (00010) that $83a9 adds to the score for each unit of time that remains.
Pointers to the 4 corner animations. $81be plays animation n when $5b,x holds $80+n.

Corner animation: column, row, width and height in cells, then frame addresses. A word below 4 is a command. Commands: 0 restarts, 1 jumps to the offset that follows, 2 starts the animation that follows, 3 stops.
Pointers to the pose sequence of each move $00-$1d. The move number is in $67,x (bit 7 set).

Move sequence: pose numbers, then $ff and a command. 0 loops, 1 sets the move to 1, 2 jumps to the offset that follows. Command 3 starts the move that follows (move $9d also turns the fighter). Other commands hold the last pose.
Moves of fighter 1 ($68) that make $893a update fighter 0 first. Else it updates fighter 1 first.
Moves that $861c and $86c2 do not change. $861c reads no joystick and $86c2 does not start move $1a.
Pointers to the pose records of poses $00-$5a. The pose number is in $6f,x.

Pose record: 9 sprite part numbers (3 x 3 grid), move flags, step size, sprite count. Part n is at $0800+64n, 0 is empty. Move flag bits 3 and 4 move the fighter by the step size. 4 bytes follow for each sprite. Sprite bytes: pointer minus $20, colour (bit 7 set: multicolour, else fighter_colours), Y position, X offset.
The 12 poses that can hit. $8825 finds the pose of the attacker here. Entry n selects hit list n.
Pointers to the hit list of each attack pose.
Hit list: pairs of defender pose and hit record number. $ff ends the list.

Hit records, 4 bytes each (39 records). $8832 reads record n at $c7ac+4n. Byte 0: distance mask (ANDed with bit_masks of the distance). Byte 1: new move of the defender, 0 for none. Byte 2: hit_sounds entry (high nibble), energy loss when not 0 (low nibble). Byte 3: hit_sprite_effects entry (high nibble), score_values entry (low nibble). 0 selects none.
The masks have only bits 0-3: only distances 0-3 hit. No hit list uses records 1, 7 and 9.
Sound requests for $dc, $dd and $de, 3 bytes each (5 entries). A zero byte leaves that request.
Hit sprite effects, 3 bytes each: sprite animation, Y position, X offset. Entry 0 is not used.
Score values, 5 digits each: 0, 500, 200, 100, 50. Entry 0 is not used.
Moves that play a sound at one step of their sequence (7 entries).
Sequence step ($69,x) of each entry of swing_sound_moves.
Sound request for $dc and $dd of each entry of swing_sound_moves.
Colour of the hires fighter sprites for each level in $be (8 entries).
Pointers to the AI column table of each level in $be (8 entries).
AI column tables, 32 bytes each. A random number (0-31) selects a column (0-7) of the AI joystick row.
Distance band (0-7) for each distance between the fighters in $aa (0-39).
Pointers to the AI row of each pose $00-$5a of the other fighter.
AI rows, 8 bytes each: one byte for each distance band. The byte selects an AI joystick row.
Row $0a. No entry of ai_row_ptrs points to this row.
No entry of ai_row_ptrs points to this row.
AI joystick rows, 8 bytes each (22 rows). $870c reads row n at $cb38+8n. Each byte is a joystick value: bits 0-3 up, down, left, right, bit 4 fire.
Row 8: the same bytes as row 4 ($cb58).
Pointers to the sprite animations $00-$15. The animation number is in $0292,x (bit 7 set).

Sprite animation: frame time, colour and flags, then sprite pointers minus $20. Flag bits: 7 multicolour, 6 wide, 5 tall. $ff and a command end it. 0 loops, 1 stops the sprite, 2 jumps to the offset that follows. 3 starts the animation that follows.
A copy of sprite_anim_04. No pointer points here.
Animations $0b-$0e: the princess of the final stage, shapes $53-$56.
Animations $0f-$14: Drax in the final stage, shapes $57-$5c.
Animation $15: the bolt that Drax throws, shapes $5d-$5f. $84ac starts it on sprite 4.
Pointers to the 4 sprite set-ups that $8e17 selects with $cb.
Figure records of the final stage: Drax stands, Drax throws, the princess, a princess variant. $8e17 selects one with final_scene_pose.
Sprite set-up, 12 bytes: animations of sprites 3-0, X positions of sprites 3-0, Y positions minus $a2.
No code writes 3 to final_scene_pose, so nothing reads this record. No other record of this table uses animation $8e (shape $56).
Start motion of the goblin (sprite 4). $84ac selects one of the 2 entries with bit 0 of the raster line.
Start motion of the bolt (sprite 4). $84ac selects one of the 2 entries with bit 0 of the raster line.
Pointers to a list of 4 moves for each goblin motion. One of these moves of fighter 0 removes the goblin.
Pointers to a list of 4 moves for each bolt motion. When fighter 0 does one of these moves, the bolt passes and stops.
Pointers to the sprite motions $00-$0b. The motion number is in $025a,x (bit 7 set).

Sprite motion: steps of 4 bytes. Directions (bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right), speeds (high nibble X, low nibble Y), frames, command. Commands: 0 next step, 1 new motion and animation follow, 2 new motion follows, 3 step follows, 4 stops. Other values: a sound request follows.
X offset of sprites 0-2 from the fighter for each facing. $9103 uses it for move $88.
Animation of sprite 0 for each facing ($9103). The 2 bytes after it are not used.
Animations of sprites 1 and 0 that $9681 starts.
Animations of sprites 4 and 3 that $96e1 starts.
Motion of sprite 0 for each facing ($9103).
Motion of sprite 1 for each facing ($9103).
Motions of sprites 1 and 0 that $9681 starts.
Motions of sprites 4 and 3 that $96e1 starts.
Pointers to the joystick direction list of each facing ($91,x).
9 joystick directions: none, forward, back, down, up, down-forward, up-forward, down-back, up-back. $8655 finds the index.
The same list for facing 1: left and right are swapped.
Move selection row of each move number when fire is not pressed.
Move selection row of each move number when fire is pressed.
Move selection rows, 9 bytes each (12 rows): the next move for each direction index of joystick_dirs. $8663 reads row n at $ce3a+9n.
Bit n for index n (8 bytes): sprite bits, voice bits and distance bits.
All bits except bit n for index n (8 bytes).
Address of each of the 9 sprite parts in the fighter buffer at $05ca. The buffer has 3 x 3 parts, 9 bytes for each line.
Offset in the fighter buffer of each of the 63 bytes of a sprite part.
Offset in the work bitmap of each byte of a fighter buffer line, from the last byte to the first. Each byte fills one cell column.
Offset of character rows 0-7 in the work bitmap (320 bytes each).
Nothing reads these bytes. They hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on.
Bitmap of the arena that is not on screen: character rows 7-22, columns 4-35, 256 bytes for each row. $8f49 swaps it with $a678-$b677 when the arena changes. The code sets $01 to $20 to read it.
Screen RAM of the arena that is not on screen, 40 bytes for each row. $8f72 swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $4400. Nothing reads the other bytes of $e000-$e3ff.
Screen RAM of the arena that is not on screen, 40 bytes for each row. $8f72 swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $4400. The hit record fault of check_attack_hit also reads $e3d9-$e3dc and $e3e1-$e3e4.
The same 24 bytes as $47e8-$47ff: the screen RAM after the screen, with the sprite pointers.
The hit record fault of check_attack_hit reads $e3ed-$e3f0 as a hit record (hit list 0, defender pose $17).
Colour RAM of the arena that is not on screen. $8f72 swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $d800. Nothing reads the other bytes of $e400-$e7ff.
Colour RAM of the arena that is not on screen. $8f72 swaps rows 7-22, columns 4-35 with $d800. The hit record fault of check_attack_hit also reads $e7e1-$e7e4.
24 bytes after the colours. Bits 0-3 are colours. Bits 4-7 vary, as in bytes read from the colour RAM, which keeps only 4 bits.
The hit record fault of check_attack_hit reads $e7ed-$e7f0 as a hit record (hit list 1, defender pose $17).
Font of the text printer, 8 bytes for each glyph (39 glyphs): space, A-Z, 0-9, "(" and ")". $9381 gives the glyph address $e800+8n. $92df makes multicolour cells from each glyph.
72 zero bytes after the font. Nothing reads them.
8 frames of the corner animations, 4 x 4 cells each (128 bytes), cell by cell and row by row. $e980-$eb7f are the right corner frames, $eb80-$ed7f the left corner frames.
Tune data of tunes $00-$56, in the RAM under the KERNAL ROM. The format is the same as at $a255.
Nothing reads these bytes. They hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on.
13 sprites. $8ddc swaps them with the sprites at $54c0-$57ff (pointers $53-$5f). $848d calls it after a won bout at level 7.
Nothing reads $ff80-$fff9. $ff80-$ffcf hold the $00/$ff fill pattern of RAM after power-on.
6502 code that writes the C128 MMU registers $ff00 and $d505, then jumps to $1100. The program does not run it.
The same bytes as freq_table at $9ff1-$a000.
$fff0-$fffe hold the same bytes as $9ff0-$9ffe in freq_table. $ffff repeats $fffe.
NMI vector. The start at $8009 writes $9519 (an RTI) here.
Reset vector RAM. The program does not use it.
IRQ vector. The start at $8009 writes $94e8 (the IRQ handler) here.
